chapters.title: The Three-Pound Universe
chapters.tease: A kilo and a half of tissue that costs a fifth of your energy and holds every memory you have.

chapters.title: How Brains Evolved
chapters.tease: Every human brain still follows a plan laid down in the oceans half a billion years ago.

chapters.title: Building a Brain
chapters.tease: Nine months turn a flat strip of cells into 86 billion neurons; the next twenty years wire them up.

chapters.title: The Neuron
chapters.tease: The cell that turned biology into information: every sensation, memory and plan runs on neurons.

chapters.title: Glia: The Other Half
chapters.tease: Once dismissed as nerve glue, glia feed, insulate, defend and prune the brain's neurons.

chapters.title: The Action Potential
chapters.tease: One code of identical spikes carries every sensation, decision and movement you will ever make.

chapters.title: The Synapse
chapters.tease: The gap between neurons is where signals become chemistry, and where learning, drugs and poisons act.

chapters.title: Chemical Messengers
chapters.tease: A handful of molecules set the brain's tone, and nearly every mind-altering drug imitates one.

chapters.title: Fuel and the Blood–Brain Barrier
chapters.tease: The brain eats a fifth of your energy but locks its door: the barrier decides what gets in.

chapters.title: Skull, Meninges and Fluid
chapters.tease: Bone, three membranes and a bath of fluid let a jelly-soft organ survive a life of bumps.

chapters.title: The Brainstem
chapters.tease: A thumb-thick stalk that breathes for you, beats your heart and switches consciousness on each morning.

chapters.title: The Cerebellum
chapters.tease: A tenth of the brain's size holding most of its neurons, it turns clumsy commands into fluent movement.

chapters.title: The Thalamus
chapters.tease: The gate through which nearly every sense reaches awareness, and the switch that closes it each night.

chapters.title: Hypothalamus and Pituitary
chapters.tease: An almond-sized region that sets temperature, hunger and thirst and commands the body's hormones.

chapters.title: The Limbic System
chapters.tease: A ring of structures where memory, motivation and emotion were found to share the same wiring.

chapters.title: The Basal Ganglia
chapters.tease: Hidden loops that choose one action from many by lifting a single brake, and fail in Parkinson's.

chapters.title: The Cerebral Cortex
chapters.tease: A crumpled sheet a few millimetres thick, built from one six-layer recipe, where perception and thought take shape.

chapters.title: The Frontal Lobes
chapters.tease: The brain's planner and brake: the source of self-control, and the last region to finish growing.

chapters.title: Two Hemispheres
chapters.tease: Cutting the bridge between the hemispheres revealed two minds in one skull, only one of which can talk.

chapters.title: The Connectome
chapters.tease: Complete wiring diagrams of brains, from a worm's 302 neurons to a whole fly, with ours still far ahead.

chapters.title: Vision: Eye to Cortex
chapters.tease: A million fibres carry the world from each eye, cross over, and are rebuilt at the back of the head.

chapters.title: Seeing Colour and Motion
chapters.tease: Colour and movement are computed in separate brain areas; lose one and the world turns grey or frozen.

chapters.title: Hearing
chapters.tease: A coiled tube 35 mm long sorts sound by pitch, and the brainstem times the ears to a hundredth of a millisecond.

chapters.title: Balance
chapters.tease: Five tiny sensors in each ear tell the brain which way is up, and a conflict with the eyes makes us sick.

chapters.title: Smell
chapters.tease: Smell is the one sense wired straight to emotion and memory, skipping the thalamus relay.

chapters.title: Taste and Flavour
chapters.tease: Five tastes, hundreds of smells and the feel of food merge into flavour, which is mostly made in the nose.

chapters.title: Touch
chapters.tease: A handful of specialist receptors, each tuned to slip, edge, buzz or caress, build the feel of the world.

chapters.title: Pain
chapters.tease: Pain is not a readout of damage but a verdict, and the brain can turn the volume down from above.

chapters.title: The Body Sense
chapters.tease: A hidden sixth sense tells you where your limbs are, and losing it means moving by sight alone.

chapters.title: The Predictive Brain
chapters.tease: The brain does not wait for the senses; it guesses first and lets the senses correct it.

chapters.title: The Motor Cortex
chapters.tease: A ridge of cortex barely a finger wide sends every voluntary command, and its map of you is wonderfully lopsided.

chapters.title: Spinal Cord and Reflexes
chapters.tease: The fastest decisions your body makes are taken in the spine, before your brain is even told.

chapters.title: Learning a Skill
chapters.tease: Practice does not just polish a movement: it hands the job to new circuits until you no longer have to think.

chapters.title: The Autonomic Nervous System
chapters.tease: An unseen network sets your heart rate, pupils and digestion every second, and both its branches are always on.

chapters.title: The Gut–Brain Axis
chapters.tease: The gut runs its own nerve net and sends the brain more messages than it receives back.

chapters.title: Hormones and the Brain
chapters.tease: Hormones turn the brain from a local network into a broadcaster that reaches every cell in the body.

chapters.title: Stress
chapters.tease: A life-saving alarm that ends in cortisol: brilliant for a sprint, corrosive when it never switches off.

chapters.title: Hunger and Appetite
chapters.tease: A rice-grain cluster of cells weighs the body's fuel and decides how hungry you feel.

chapters.title: Mirror Neurons
chapters.tease: Cells that fire when you act and when you watch: a genuine discovery that became one of neuroscience's great myths.

chapters.title: The Brain and the Immune System
chapters.tease: The brain is not walled off from the immune system: it listens to infection, and makes you feel ill on purpose.

chapters.title: Patient H.M. and the Hippocampus
chapters.tease: One operation in 1953 took away a man's future memories and showed that memory is made of separate systems.

chapters.title: Kinds of Memory
chapters.tease: Memory is not one store but a family of systems, which is why an amnesic can forget his lessons yet keep the skill.

chapters.title: Working Memory
chapters.tease: The mind's workspace holds about four things at once, and almost every thought must squeeze through it.

chapters.title: How a Memory Is Made
chapters.tease: Memory is written by strengthening synapses, and in 2012 scientists switched a single memory back on with light.

chapters.title: Forgetting
chapters.tease: Most of what we learn is gone within a day, and that ruthless pruning is what keeps memory useful.

chapters.title: False Memories
chapters.tease: Every time you recall a memory you rebuild it, and a few words from a stranger can help you rebuild it wrong.

chapters.title: Habits
chapters.tease: Habits hand everyday behaviour from conscious choice to a loop deep in the brain, freeing the mind and binding it.

chapters.title: Neuroplasticity
chapters.tease: The adult brain rewires itself with practice: cabbies grow their hippocampus and jugglers their motion areas.

chapters.title: Sleep and Memory
chapters.tease: While you sleep, the hippocampus replays the day at high speed and hands its lessons to the cortex.

chapters.title: Expertise
chapters.tease: Experts do not have better memories; they have bigger chunks, built from thousands of hours of focused practice.

chapters.title: Fear and the Amygdala
chapters.tease: A small almond of nuclei can make you leap before you think, and it can learn a new fear in a single lesson.

chapters.title: Reward and Dopamine
chapters.tease: Dopamine does not reward you for pleasure; it fires for surprise, and teaches the brain what to chase next.

chapters.title: Love and Bonding
chapters.tease: One vole mates for life and its cousin never does; the difference lies in a handful of brain receptors.

chapters.title: Empathy
chapters.tease: We wince when others are hurt, but the brain's sharing is narrow, biased and, luckily, trainable.

chapters.title: Making Decisions
chapters.tease: A man with a perfect IQ could not choose a date for lunch, and his case showed that feeling is part of reason.

chapters.title: Phineas Gage
chapters.tease: An iron bar through the head made one railway foreman the most famous patient in brain science.

chapters.title: Attention
chapters.tease: The brain throws away most of what the senses send, and a gorilla can walk past unnoticed.

chapters.title: Consciousness
chapters.tease: Neuroscience can now detect hidden awareness in a silent patient, yet still cannot say why anything is felt.

chapters.title: The Sense of Self
chapters.tease: Stroke a rubber hand in sync with your own and within minutes your brain adopts it; the self is an inference.

chapters.title: Free Will
chapters.tease: A wrist flick, a clock and a scalp electrode started a 40-year argument about whether we choose at all.

chapters.title: Broca and Wernicke
chapters.tease: Two damaged brains in 1860s Europe proved that language lives in particular places, mostly on the left.

chapters.title: The Reading Brain
chapters.tease: Reading is too new to have evolved, so every literate brain repurposes visual cortex built for spotting objects.

chapters.title: The Number Sense
chapters.tease: Babies, monkeys and bees sense quantity without words; exact arithmetic is a cultural tool layered on top.

chapters.title: Music and the Brain
chapters.tease: Music lights up hearing, movement, memory and reward at once, which is why it moves us and helps heal us.

chapters.title: The Bilingual Brain
chapters.tease: Two languages share one brain, held apart by a control network that never stops choosing which word to use.

chapters.title: Intelligence
chapters.tease: A century of testing found one general factor behind mental skills, and a frontal-parietal network to carry it.

chapters.title: Creativity
chapters.tease: The aha moment has a brain signature: a quiet pause, then a burst of activity over the right temporal lobe.

chapters.title: The Default Mode Network
chapters.tease: When you stop concentrating, a network of brain hubs switches on to remember, plan and think about yourself.

chapters.title: Self-Control
chapters.tease: The marshmallow test made waiting famous; newer studies show trust, strategy and background matter as much as grit.

chapters.title: Brain Myths
chapters.tease: Neuromyths spread through classrooms and films; each one hides a truer and more interesting fact about the brain.

chapters.title: Why We Sleep
chapters.tease: Sleep is no shutdown: the brain runs a timed programme each night that cleans, sorts and resets it.

chapters.title: The Body Clock
chapters.tease: A tiny cluster of neurons above the optic nerves keeps time for every organ, and daylight sets it each morning.

chapters.title: Dreams
chapters.tease: Every night the brain runs a vivid simulation while switching off the muscles that might act it out.

chapters.title: Sleep Disorders
chapters.tease: Sleep can fail in dozens of ways, from a collapsing airway to missing brain cells, and most can be treated.

chapters.title: Anaesthesia
chapters.tease: Doctors switch consciousness off and on millions of times a day, and the science of how is still unfolding.

chapters.title: Coma and Brain Death
chapters.tease: Between waking and death lie several states of consciousness, and some hide an aware mind inside a still body.

chapters.title: Meditation
chapters.tease: Meditation trains one small skill, catching the mind as it wanders, and the brain networks behind it.

chapters.title: Psychedelics
chapters.tease: A rye-fungus chemical and a Mexican mushroom opened a window on how the brain builds the sense of self.

chapters.title: Caffeine, Alcohol and Nicotine
chapters.tease: Three ordinary drugs, sold in cafés, pubs and shops, each fit a different lock in the brain.

chapters.title: Addiction
chapters.tease: Addictive drugs hijack the brain's teaching signal until wanting outlasts liking and control wears thin.

chapters.title: Stroke
chapters.tease: Every minute a large stroke goes untreated, around 1.9 million neurons die, so speed became medicine.

chapters.title: Epilepsy
chapters.tease: Epilepsy surgery let doctors stimulate and record the living human brain, and gave us its first maps.

chapters.title: Concussion
chapters.tease: A knock that shows nothing on a scan can still trigger a chemical crisis inside the brain.

chapters.title: Alzheimer's Disease
chapters.tease: The disease starts decades before forgetting, which turns early detection and prevention into the battleground.

chapters.title: Parkinson's Disease
chapters.tease: Finding that dopamine loss causes Parkinson's gave medicine its first drug that replaces a missing brain chemical.

chapters.title: Multiple Sclerosis
chapters.tease: Multiple sclerosis showed that the immune system can attack the brain's own wiring, and that it can be stopped.

chapters.title: Depression
chapters.tease: Depression proved that mood has a biology, and that talk, drugs and electricity can all change it.

chapters.title: Schizophrenia
chapters.tease: The first antipsychotic emptied asylums and led to the dopamine theory, the first chemical model of a mental illness.

chapters.title: Neurodiversity
chapters.tease: Neurodiversity reframed autism, ADHD and dyslexia as differences in wiring that call for understanding, not only cure.

chapters.title: Migraine
chapters.tease: Migraine is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and decoding it led to the first drugs designed for it.

chapters.title: Cajal and the Neuron Doctrine
chapters.tease: Cajal showed the brain is built from separate cells, the idea every later discovery about neurons rests on.

chapters.title: Brainwaves
chapters.tease: The EEG let doctors watch a living brain's electrical rhythms, and it still diagnoses epilepsy and stages sleep.

chapters.title: Brain Scanning
chapters.tease: Scanners turned the living brain from a sealed box into something doctors can see and measure every day.

chapters.title: Optogenetics
chapters.tease: Light-gated proteins let scientists switch chosen neurons on or off in milliseconds, testing what each circuit does.

chapters.title: Brain–Computer Interfaces
chapters.tease: Implants that read motor cortex let paralysed people move cursors and robot arms, and speak again.

chapters.title: Deep Brain Stimulation
chapters.tease: A battery and a wire can calm tremor and stiffness by retuning a misfiring circuit deep inside the brain.

chapters.title: Brains and AI
chapters.tease: Artificial neural networks began as a sketch of the neuron, and now help explain the brain that inspired them.

chapters.title: Animal Minds
chapters.tease: Octopuses, crows and bees evolved clever brains separately, proving the cortex is only one recipe for a mind.

chapters.title: The Teenage and Ageing Brain
chapters.tease: The brain rebuilds itself across a lifetime, from teenage pruning to the reserve that protects old age.

chapters.title: The Future Brain
chapters.tease: Organoids, connectomes and implants are reshaping neuroscience, and forcing new laws to protect the mind.
